title: Simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
authors: Huan-Yu Liu, Cheng Xue, Yun-Jie Wang, Xi-Ning Zhuang, Chao Wang, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Guo-Ping Guo
abstract: Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors. In this work, we propose a resource-efficient algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum $XY$ model demonstrate the accuracy and resource efficiency of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.
summary: This paper presents a resource-efficient algorithm to simulate open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware by addressing the challenges posed by non-unitary dissipation. It achieves this by first using a stable adjoint channel representation and then introducing an adaptive variational compression technique to drastically reduce the circuit depth required for repeated Hamiltonian evolution steps.
main_problem: Developing a resource-efficient algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices.
main_result: The proposed method achieves ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, demonstrated successfully on the dissipative quantum XY model.
method: It combines deriving a stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel approximation for dissipation with an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework to replace deep unitary segments.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum system governed by the Lindblad master equation, focusing specifically on dynamics involving Pauli dissipations ($P_k \in \{I, X, Y, Z\}^{\otimes n}$).
key_observables: Accuracy of simulation (approximating evolution over $\delta t$), resource efficiency, and circuit depth reduction.
important_parameters: Dissipation rates ($\gamma_k$), time step ($\delta t$), and the compression parameters ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve approximating the dynamics via a stable adjoint channel and using variational circuits to approximate repeated Trotterized Hamiltonian evolution operators.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the entire process: (a) Lindbladian dynamics; (b) Adjoint channel formulation; (c) Variational circuit compression training setup; (d) Monte Carlo sampling with PQC insertion ($ ar{U}_{r_a}$); and (e) Simulation using compressed trajectories.
paper_structure: The paper first addresses the challenge of NISQ simulation for open systems, derives a stable adjoint channel to avoid classical post-processing, and then introduces the adaptive variational compression framework to reduce circuit depth by replacing repeated unitary blocks with trained PQCs. Finally, it validates this approach on the XY model.
why_interesting: This work directly tackles the major practical bottleneck in quantum simulation of open systems—circuit depth—by integrating advanced techniques from both quantum control (adjoint channels) and variational quantum algorithms (compression).
